question: Will Donald Trump announce a presidential run before 2027?
thesis: Structural read, not live news. A third-term run is barred by the 22nd Amendment; the only YES path is a resolver counting a troll remark ('Trump 2028' hats, 'I'd love to') as an announcement that he is running in 2028. The criteria require an announcement that he IS running, and Trump's own stated line has been that he is 'not allowed' to run. The residual is definitional risk on a joke, priced here at 3%; the market's 6.45% carries a resolution-ambiguity premium I judge too high. Correlated with the frozen 692259/692265 'nobody announces a 2028 run in 2026' thesis.

Correlated with the frozen 'no 2028 announcements in 2026' cluster.

question: Will Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez announce a Presidential run before 2027?
thesis: Structural read. Ocasio-Cortez is a serious 2028 name, but no major-party contender has announced a presidential run before the midterm year closes in modern cycles except Trump (15 Nov 2022, as a former president), and she is on the ballot for her House seat on 3 Nov 2026. The realistic window is Nov-Dec 2026 and her incentive is to hold optionality (Senate 2028 vs presidency) into 2027. 3% vs 7.5c. Correlated with the frozen Newsom/Harris entries.

question: Will J.D. Vance announce a presidential run before 2027?
thesis: Structural read. Sitting VPs announce in the year after the midterms (Bush Jun 1999, Gore Jun 1999, Biden Apr 2019); announcing during 2026 would step on the president's midterm campaign and Trump has kept the Vance-vs-Rubio question deliberately open. Vance is the likeliest name in the cluster to announce early, so the disagreement with the crowd is small (3.5% vs 5.5c) and this is frozen mainly for calibration of the low-probability bucket.

question: Zelenskyy out as Ukraine president by end of 2026?
thesis: Coherence read against my own frozen ledger: I hold 'Ukraine election held by 31 Dec 2026' at 2.5% (677358) and 'peace deal before 2027' at 18% (665224). Zelenskyy leaving office inside 2026 requires resignation, removal, death or an election-and-transfer; martial law blocks the election path and even a H2-2026 peace deal leaves too little calendar for an election plus inauguration before 31 Dec. The non-election paths (resignation as a peace-deal concession, or health/violence) are the 4%. The market's 6.5c is above what the election-path arithmetic and my other two frozen legs support.

question: Will Brad Bradford win the 2026 Toronto mayoral election?
thesis: Coherence read: I froze Olivia Chow at 89% (1812607), so the complement left for all challengers is ~11%; Bradford (Beaches-East York councillor, centre-right) is the most credible of them but the anti-Chow vote historically splits across several right-of-centre candidates (Bailao/Saunders/Bradford in 2023), and an incumbent mayor with a plurality base in a one-round FPTP race is hard to beat. 7% for Bradford, leaving ~4% for the field. This is the same view as the frozen Chow leg, not independent evidence.

question: Will CDU win less than 8% of all valid second votes?
thesis: Mecklenburg-Vorpommern Landtag, 20 Sep 2026. Structural prior: CDU MV has never polled below its 2021 floor of 13.3% (2016 19.0%, 2011 23.0%); late-2025 MV polling had CDU at roughly 12-15% behind AfD and SPD. For a sub-8% result the party must shed 5+ points from its historical floor. The crowd at 29.5% implies mid-2026 polling near 9-11%, which I cannot see (stale-prior caveat, hence low confidence and q shaded from a raw ~10% toward the market). Even taking the crowd's implied poll level, a 2.5-pt polling sd puts P(<8%) near 15-20%, not 30%. Thin book (21k), so the price is also less informative than the liquid legs I froze on this election (1364103/1364105).

question: Will Grüne win the most seats in the 2026 Berlin state elections?
thesis: Berlin Abgeordnetenhaus, 20 Sep 2026. Grüne finished second in 2021 (18.9%) and 2023 (18.4%) but the market has Linke 54% / CDU 29% for most seats, i.e. Linke has surged past Grüne on the left (consistent with Linke topping Berlin in the Feb 2025 federal vote). For Grüne to finish first they must overtake both CDU and a surging Linke inside three weeks; that is a 1-2% event. Small disagreement, frozen mainly for the low-probability calibration bucket; sits beside the frozen AfD-most-seats Berlin leg (789953).

question: Will ACA premium tax credits not be extended and will the Democratic Party win the House in 2026?
thesis: Conjunction market. Leg 1 ('enhanced ACA credits extended in 2025?') resolved NO in fact -- the enhanced credits lapsed on 31 Dec 2025 and the House's Jan 2026 extension vote came after the 2025 deadline -- so this market collapses to 'Democrats win the House in 2026' with a small residual for a resolver crediting a retroactive 2025 extension (~3%). I froze D-House at 83% vs the crowd's 88.5% (562802), so coherence gives 0.83 x 0.97 ~ 0.80 here. This is a re-expression of the frozen House view, not independent evidence; the sibling 902971 (R-House conjunction) is deliberately NOT frozen to avoid double-counting one view a second time.
